title: Option Compare Text makes '=' string comparisons case-INSENSITIVE — a naive C# '==' port silently changes matching behaviour
sourceContent:
Option Compare Text   ' <-- ALL string '=' comparisons in this file are case-INSENSITIVE

Public Class LoginValidator
    ' Under Option Compare Text, "ADMIN" = "admin" is TRUE.
    ' Ported naively to C# as (role == "admin"), "ADMIN" returns FALSE -> auth bug.
    Public Function IsAdmin(role As String) As Boolean
        Return role = "admin"
    End Function

    Public Function SameUser(a As String, b As String) As Boolean
        Return a = b   ' case-insensitive under Option Compare Text
    End Function
End Class
notes: Option Compare Text (file- or project-level) makes every unqualified '=' string comparison case-insensitive. C# '==' is always ordinal/case-sensitive, so a mechanical port flips the result for mixed-case input. The extractor must flag every string '=' under Option Compare Text and require an explicit StringComparison choice (OrdinalIgnoreCase vs InvariantCultureIgnoreCase) in the C# target.
